hero.title: Birth and Life of Mahavira (540-468 BC)
hero.description: An interactive study guide on Vardhamana Mahavira: his lineage (Jnatrika Kshatriyas), Trishala, early life, 12 years of asceticism, enlightenment (Kevala Jnana) at Rijupalika, First Sermon, Gandharas, and Nirvana at Pavapuri.

timeline.title: Vardhamana Mahavira's Life Journey
timeline.description: Chronological progression of the key events in the life of the 24th Tirthankara.

cards.details: Born as Vardhamana to Siddhartha (Chief of Jnatrika Kshatriyas) and Trishala (Lichchhavi princess) near Vaishali, Bihar.
Left home at the age of 30 to lead an ascetic life, wandering and practicing severe self-mortification for 12 years.
Attained omniscience under a Sal tree on the banks of River Rijupalika near Jrimbhikagrama at the age of 42.
Passed away at the age of 72 in Pavapuri (near Nalanda, Bihar) under the patronage of King Hastipala.

toolEvolution.title: Four Stages of Mahavira's Life
toolEvolution.description: The spiritual transformation from a prince of Vaishali to the Jina (Conqueror).

stages.name: Princehood (Vardhamana)
stages.desc: Born into the royal Jnatrika Kshatriya clan. Married Yashoda and had a daughter, Anojja.

stages.name: Asceticism (Sadhana)
stages.desc: Renounced worldly life at 30. Practiced rigorous penance and wandered naked. Met Makkhali Gosala.

stages.name: Omniscience (Kevala Jnana)
stages.desc: Conquered all desires. Became a Jina (Conqueror) on the banks of Rijupalika River.

stages.name: Preaching & Sangha
stages.desc: Preached in Magadha/Kosala. Led 11 main disciples (Gandharas) and attained Nirvana at Pavapuri.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Trap: Confusing Mahavira as the founder of Jainism. Remember he was the 24th Tirthankara; the first was Rishabhanatha (Adinatha) and the 23rd was Parshvanatha.

Trap: Swapping family lineages. Mahavira's father belonged to the Jnatrika clan, and his mother Trishala was a Lichchhavi princess (sister of King Chetaka). UPSC often swaps these with Buddha's Shakya/Koliya parents.
Trap: Confusing River Rijupalika (where Mahavira attained Kevala Jnana) with River Niranjana (Lilajan) where Buddha attained Enlightenment.

Trap: Thinking that Mahavira formulated all five vows of Jainism. Parsvanatha had already preached four (Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya, Aparigraha). Mahavira only added the fifth vow, Brahmacharya (chastity).
Trap: Misidentifying Pavapuri (place of Mahavira's death/Nirvana) with Kusinara/Kushinagar (place of Buddha's death/Mahaparinirvana). Both are heavily tested.

items.question: What was the birth name of Lord Mahavira?
Who was Makkhali Gosala and what was his relationship with Mahavira?
items.answer: He was the founder of the Ajivika sect who accompanied Mahavira as a disciple/ascetic partner for six years before separating due to doctrinal differences.

items.question: Where did Mahavira attain Kevala Jnana and under which tree?
items.answer: On the banks of the Rijupalika River near Jrimbhikagrama village, under a Sal tree.

items.question: Who were the 'Gandharas' in early Jainism?
items.answer: The eleven chief disciples of Mahavira who helped organize and spread the Jain teachings and monastic order.

items.question: Where did Mahavira attain Nirvana and under whose political patronage?
items.answer: At Pavapuri (near Nalanda, Bihar) in 468 BCE, under the patronage of the Malla King Hastipala.

deepDive.title: Vardhamana Mahavira: Biography & Historical Impact
deepDive.description: A comprehensive UPSC study notes on the birth, family, spiritual wandering, Kevala Jnana, and final liberation of the 24th Jain Tirthankara.

sections.title: 1. Lineage, Birth and Early Life of Vardhamana
sections.content:
Vardhamana was born in 540 BCE at Kundagrama, a suburb of the ancient city of Vaishali (in modern Muzaffarpur district, Bihar). He belonged to the royal Jnatrika Kshatriya clan. His father, Siddhartha, was the head of this clan, and his mother, Trishala, was a Lichchhavi princess and sister of Chetaka, the ruler of Vaishali.

Vardhamana led a comfortable household life. He was married to Yashoda and had a daughter named Anojja (also known as Priyadarsana). His daughter married Jamali, who later became Mahavira's first disciple but also led the first internal split (schism) in Jainism.

sections.title: 2. Renunciation and 12 Years of Spiritual Sadhana
sections.content:
At the age of 30, following the death of his parents, Vardhamana renounced his royal household, wealth, and family. He left home to seek ultimate truth. He spent the next 12 years wandering as a homeless ascetic, practicing severe self-mortification, fasting, and meditation. He eventually discarded all clothing to practice absolute detachment.

During the second year of his wandering, he met Makkhali Gosala at Nalanda. Gosala accompanied Mahavira for six years as his close disciple. However, differences arose regarding the doctrine of fate and destiny, leading Gosala to separate and establish the Ajivika sect, which preached fatalism (Niyati).

sections.title: 3. Kevala Jnana: Enlightenment on the Rijupalika River
sections.content:
At the age of 42, after 12 years of intense penance, Vardhamana attained Kevala Jnana (omniscience or absolute supreme knowledge). This event took place outside the village of Jrimbhikagrama, under a sacred Sal tree, on the banks of the Rijupalika River.

Mahavira's Post-Enlightenment Epithets

TitleLiteral MeaningSignificance in Jainism
JinaConquerorOne who has conquered all worldly desires, senses, and passions.
MahaviraGreat HeroRepresenting his supreme courage and endurance in practicing penance.
KevalinOmniscientPossessor of absolute, infinite, supreme knowledge (Kevala Jnana).
NigranthaFree from bondsOne who is completely detached from all material ties and possessiveness.

Following this enlightenment, Mahavira spent the remaining 30 years of his life traveling across eastern India—primarily Magadha, Anga, Kosala, Mithila, and Champa—preaching his doctrines and organizing his monastic order.

Key Tirthankaras & Emblems (UPSC High-Yield)

Jain tradition speaks of 24 Tirthankaras (spiritual teachers). Rigveda makes references to two Tirthankaras—Rishabhadeva (1st) and Arishtanemi (22nd). UPSC frequently tests their associated animal emblems in match-the-following questions:

TirthankaraPositionEmblem (Lanchana)
Rishabhanatha (Adinatha)1st Tirthankara🐂 Bull (Vrishabha)
Mallinatha19th Tirthankara🏺 Water Jar (Kalasha)
Neminatha22nd Tirthankara🐚 Conch Shell (Shankha)
Parshvanatha23rd Tirthankara🐍 Serpent (Sarpa)
Mahavira (Vardhamana)24th Tirthankara🦁 Lion (Simha)

sections.title: 4. Preaching, Monastic Sangha, and Nirvana at Pavapuri
sections.content:
Mahavira delivered his first sermon at Vipulachala Hill in Rajgriha. He organized a disciplined monastic community (Sangha) and attracted 11 chief disciples, known as the Gandharas (or Ganadharas). Only one Gandhara, Sudharma, survived Mahavira and became the first head of the Jain church after him.

Mahavira adopted the four vows preached by the 23rd Tirthankara, Parshvanatha (Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya, Aparigraha), and added the fifth vow: Brahmacharya (Chastity).

In 468 BCE, at the age of 72, Vardhamana Mahavira attained Nirvana (final liberation/death) at Pavapuri (modern Nalanda district, Bihar). He passed away in the palace of the Malla King Hastipala. Pavapuri remains one of the holiest pilgrimage sites (Siddha-kshetra) for Jains worldwide.

Royal Patronage & Contemporary Monarchs

Vardhamana Mahavira established strong relations with the contemporary ruling dynasties of Magadha and surrounding regions, which helped in the state patronage and protection of the Jain Sangha:

  • Magadha (Haryanka Dynasty): King Bimbisara and King Ajatashatru were contemporaries who actively patronized and respected both Mahavira and Buddha.
  • Vaishali (Lichchhavis): King Chetaka, the republic chief and Mahavira's maternal uncle, provided political patronage in the Vajji confederacy.
  • Avanti (Pradyota Dynasty): King Pradyota of Ujjain was a strong follower who facilitated the spread of Jainism in Western India.
  • Mallas: The republic under whom Mahavira attained Nirvana at Pavapuri in King Hastipala's territory.
